speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of high fever, seizures, and a generalized nonpruritic rash; tell me, when did your fever first start and how high did it go?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)

The clinical picture of a high fever (40.5°C) lasting five days followed by a seizure and the subsequent appearance of a generalized nonpruritic rash that started on the trunk is classic for Roseola, caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 or 7. Given the infant's age and the sequence of symptoms, do you have any questions about the treatment plan or the prognosis?
